status: accepted after four targeted wording clarifications
blind_method: Only id/concept/prerequisites/prompt/options were displayed before expected answers and mathematics were written and hashed. Answer, explanation and transfer fields were first inspected after the freeze. Transfers and guide were reviewed afterward; no blind-transfer claim is made.

items.mathematics: The favorable equally likely outcomes are {6,7,8}; 3 of 8 outcomes qualify.
items.distractor_review: 1/8 counts only 6; 3/5 uses unfavorable outcomes as denominator; 5/8 is the complement.
items.transfer_derivation: Need the masses of the favorable outcomes, or other information sufficient to determine their sum. Equal labels do not imply equal probabilities.

items.mathematics: The two stated categories are exhaustive and disjoint, so P(no rework)=1-27/100=73/100.
items.distractor_review: 0.27 repeats the given event; 0.37 and 0.63 do not complement 0.27.
items.transfer_derivation: The literal complement is not missing the deadline. 'Meeting the deadline' is equivalent under the guide's explicit exhaustive two-way interpretation.

items.mathematics: The union contains 30+24-12=42 distinct learners; uniform selection gives 42/60=7/10.
items.distractor_review: 0.90 double-counts the overlap; 0.50 counts drawing only; 0.20 counts the intersection.
items.transfer_derivation: The union has 42 learners, so 60-42=18; alternatively (1-0.70)*60=18.

items.mathematics: Conditioning restricts the equally likely sample space to 30 Windows builds, of which 6 failed: 6/30=1/5.
items.distractor_review: 0.06 is the joint share among all builds; 0.60 reverses the conditioning (Windows among failed); 0.80 is Windows success.
items.transfer_derivation: Condition on the 70 Linux builds, with 4 failures: 4/70=2/35. This describes uniform selection from the stated finite log.

items.mathematics: There are 30 late parcels and 18 of them are priority, so P(priority|late)=18/30=3/5.
items.distractor_review: 0.30 reverses the conditioning (18/60); 0.075 is the joint fraction (18/240); 0.25 is the marginal priority share (60/240).
items.transfer_derivation: For late given priority, the joint numerator remains 18 but the conditioning group has 60 parcels: 18/60=3/10.

items.mathematics: After the known first red token is removed, 2 red and 2 blue remain. Conditional probability for the second draw is 2/4=1/2.
items.distractor_review: 3/5 ignores the first removal; 2/5 updates only the numerator; 3/4 treats the first removed token as blue.
items.transfer_derivation: Replacement restores the original three red and two blue tokens. The original uniform-draw condition carries through the counterfactual.

items.distractor_review: Unequal marginal probabilities, an intersection smaller than each marginal, and a marginal sum below one do not establish dependence or independence.
items.transfer_derivation: 0.3/0.5=0.6 differs from P(A)=0.4. The changed joint model is feasible: cells 0.3,0.1,0.2,0.4 are nonnegative and sum to one.

items.mathematics: Mutual exclusivity implies P(A and B)=0, whereas P(A)P(B)=0.3*0.2=0.06>0. Since P(B)>0, P(A|B)=0 differs from P(A)=0.3.
items.distractor_review: Never occurring together does provide information; a valid sum is irrelevant; the claim that every pair of different events changes probabilities is false even though its opening 'No' matches the classification.
items.transfer_derivation: A={1,2,3}, B={9,10}. Joint probability 0 differs from (3/10)(2/10)=3/50, and P(A|B)=0 differs from 3/10.

items.mathematics: Independence gives P(neither)=0.90*0.80=0.72, so P(at least one)=1-0.72=0.28=7/25. Also 0.10+0.20-0.02=0.28.
items.distractor_review: 0.02 is both failures; 0.30 treats failure events as mutually exclusive; 0.70 complements that incorrect sum.
items.transfer_answer: P(A union B)=0.30-q where q=P(A and B)
items.transfer_derivation: The joint overlap suffices. Equivalently use P(B|A)*P(A) or P(A|B)*P(B) for q. Independence is not licensed in this counterfactual.

items.mathematics: P(B and defective)=0.40*0.06=0.024. Total defective probability is 0.60*0.02+0.40*0.06=0.036. Their ratio is 0.024/0.036=2/3.
items.distractor_review: 1/3 is the posterior for A; 2/5 is B's prior share; 3/4 normalizes the defect rates while ignoring unequal workshop shares.

items.mathematics: P(defective and flagged)=0.01*0.90=0.009. P(nondeffective and flagged)=0.99*0.10=0.099. The posterior is 0.009/(0.009+0.099)=1/12.
items.distractor_review: 9/10 is the sensitivity, 1/10 is the false-positive rate, and 1/100 is the prior; none is the requested posterior.
items.transfer_derivation: The joint event uses all 1,000 equally weighted model files, whereas the original posterior conditions on the 108 flagged files.

items.mathematics: With prevalence p, the posterior is 0.9p/(0.9p+0.1(1-p))=9p/(1+8p). At p=0.01 this is 1/12; at p=0.10 it is 1/2. Fixed positive flag rates make this increase with p.
items.distractor_review: The sensitivity 9/10 and false-positive rate 1/10 do not become the posterior. An increasing prior cannot produce the stated decrease when both conditional flag rates stay fixed.
items.transfer_derivation: At prevalence 1/2, posterior=0.45/(0.45+0.05)=0.90. The prior weights both contributions to total flags; conditional rates are unchanged.

graph.assessment: The concept graph matches the mathematical relationships. Fractions, percentages and multiplication are the externally stated entry prerequisites; the graph is not claimed to enforce a fixed display sequence.

guide_review.app_behavior_qualification: Import, selection/shuffling, feedback, completion, trace and note-download behavior remain a separate receiving phase; this content review does not assert a browser run.

Guide section references and mathematical definitions match the primary reading. No exercises or source text were copied into this review.

limitations: Mathematical/editorial content acceptance, not evidence of learning effectiveness
